titleText.es: El veto de la UAI vino después del incidente
titleText.en: The IAU ban came after the 'redefinition of 'planet' to include the IAU president's mom' incident.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive metadata is truncated after incidente because the page places unescaped quotation marks inside its HTML title attribute. The page continues with the same invented planet-redefinition insult preserved in the complete official English title text; UAI is the Spanish abbreviation for the International Astronomical Union, called the IAU in English.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: welcome (addressing a mixed or all-male group)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bienvenidos is the masculine plural form of bienvenido. Use bienvenidas for an all-female group.
Charla can mean a spoken presentation for an audience. That is distinct from its conversational sense, where it means an informal chat or discussion.

example.es: Marta dio una charla sobre astronomía.
example.en: Marta gave a talk about astronomy.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you all are (informal plural, mainly in Spain)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sois is the present form of ser used with vosotros or vosotras, the informal way to address several people in Spain.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; links ‘some’ to the larger group
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After algunos or algunas, de introduces the group from which the smaller set is chosen. Spanish normally keeps the matching article before that group: algunos de los, algunas de las.

example.es: Algunas de las ventanas están abiertas.
example.en: Some of the windows are open.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Brillante can describe a bright light or, figuratively, a very intelligent or impressive person. Its plural is brillantes for every gender.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to speak to you all (informal plural, mainly in Spain)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hablaros joins hablar, the unchanged dictionary form meaning ‘to speak,’ with os, the short word for several people addressed informally in Spain.

example.en: I want to speak to you all about an idea.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: your (informal plural in Spain; before one feminine thing)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vuestra says that something belongs to several people addressed informally. Its feminine singular ending matches the one feminine thing owned, not the number or gender of the owners.
Paréntesis is written the same way in singular and plural. Context words reveal the number: un paréntesis is one parenthesis, while dos paréntesis is two parentheses.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks the ‘come to mind’ use of ocurrir
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In the pattern se me/te/le/nos/os/les ocurre, se is required before the short word naming the person who has the idea. It does not mean that the idea acts on itself.
With se and a short recipient word such as me or le, ocurre presents an idea as coming to someone rather than simply reporting that an event happens.
The prefix des- reverses compensado here: the parts no longer look balanced or well matched.

example.en: The drawing ended up looking unbalanced.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: from; at (introducing where a ban applies)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After estar vetado, en introduces the place, event, or setting where the ban applies. Natural English often uses ‘from’ or ‘at’ rather than the usual literal ‘in.’

example.en: He is banned from several stadiums.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the feminine plural article inside las que (‘which’)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After a preposition, las can join que to refer back to feminine plural things. Las matches those things; que itself does not change.

example.es: Son las salas en las que trabajamos.
example.en: They are the rooms that we work in.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vetado is the masculine singular completed-action form of vetar. After estar, it describes the resulting state of being barred.
Canadiense has the same singular form for masculine and feminine nouns.
Here convención means an organized event or gathering. The same word can also mean an agreed practice or rule, which is a different sense.

example.es: La ciudad recibe varias convenciones cada año.
example.en: The city hosts several conventions each year.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: furry; related to fans of anthropomorphic animal characters
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish commonly borrows the English word furry for this subculture. When it modifies an event or group, it is often left unchanged for gender and number.

example.es: Hay una convención furry este fin de semana.
example.en: There is a furry convention this weekend.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: EEUU abbreviates Estados Unidos. The repeated E and U show that both words are plural; formal writing often adds periods and a space as EE. UU.

example.es: La empresa vende sus productos en EEUU.
example.en: The company sells its products in the US.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Repostera can describe something connected with making cakes, pastries, and other sweets. Its feminine ending matches a feminine singular noun.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say ‘some of’ a named group?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use algunos or algunas, then de, then los or las and the group.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Choose algunos before a masculine or mixed set and algunas before a feminine set. Los or las agrees with the larger group that follows. This pattern selects a smaller set from that larger group.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that doing something is an honor?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use es un honor, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir, such as hablar, conocer, or recibir. Es can change when the time changes, but the action verb after honor stays in that dictionary form.

example.en: It is an honor to meet you.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that text is written in parentheses?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Entre usually means ‘between,’ but this conventional expression describes words placed between an opening and a closing parenthesis. Paréntesis has the same written form for one parenthesis and for more than one.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that an idea occurs to someone or comes to mind?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put se before me, te, le, nos, os, or les, then use ocurre for one idea or ocurren for several.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short word after se identifies who has the idea: me for me, te for informal you, le for one other person or formal you, nos for us, os for informal plural you in Spain, and les for several other people. The verb agrees with the idea, not with that person: ocurre una idea but ocurren dos ideas.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why can a parenthetical statement ending in an emoticon look ambiguous?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: One closing parenthesis can look like both the smile's mouth and the end of the parenthetical text; adding another clarifies the structure but can make the face look odd.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The two rejected versions trade grammatical clarity against visual balance. The joke treats this tiny punctuation problem as an urgent topic for a prestigious talk.

regions.labelEs: SOIS ALGUNOS DE LOS INNOVADORES MÁS BRILLANTES, DE MUCHOS CAMPOS, ES UN HONOR HABLAROS DE UN PROBLEMA QUE NECESITA DESESPERADAMENTE DE VUESTRA ATENCIÓN:

applications.explanationEn: Sois is the present form of ser for the several people addressed informally in the form used mainly in Spain.
Algunos selects a masculine or mixed subset, and de los introduces the larger group named by innovadores.
This de connects algunos to the larger group from which that subset is selected.
Los matches the plural group, innovadores names it, and más brillantes marks the highest degree of the description.
Problema names the thing being described, que links it to the added information, and necesita supplies the verb inside that description.
Es un honor introduces the respectful evaluation, and hablaros supplies the following action in its unchanged dictionary form.
Os is attached directly to the unchanged verb hablar and identifies the several people addressed.
The attached os refers to several people addressed informally, a form used mainly in Spain.
Desesperada takes the ending -mente to form a word describing the urgent manner or degree of the need.
This de introduces what is required after necesita; natural English absorbs the relationship into the verb ‘need’ or ‘require.’
Vuestra addresses several people informally and uses feminine singular agreement for the one feminine thing possessed.

regions.labelEs: ¿CÓMO CERRAR CON UN EMOTICONO UN ENUNCIADO ENTRE PARÉNTESIS?

applications.explanationEn: Cómo asks for the unknown method and keeps its written accent; cerrar stays in its unchanged -ar dictionary form.
Entre and paréntesis form the conventional writing expression for material placed between the two punctuation marks.

regions.labelEs: NO SE ME OCURRE UNA BUENA FORMA.

applications.exampleEs: SE ME OCURRE UNA BUENA FORMA
applications.explanationEn: Se marks the come-to-mind pattern, me identifies the person receiving the idea, ocurre agrees with one idea, and una buena forma fills that idea slot.
